title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
abstract: arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. translated_title: Token去哪儿了：智能体编程中的热量、熵与误差
translated_abstract: 编程智能体按token计费，然而软件工程从未说明一个token究竟能买到什么。在此，我们提出了一种软件热力学理论。该理论借鉴经典热力学与随机热力学中的类比并加以扩展，将其应用于现代智能体编程。我们将智能体生成的token数计为其成本，并把该成本划分为功与热。测试套件则扮演软件版麦克斯韦妖的角色，评判每一次代码变更。我们通过类比“将单个分子拉开再让其重新折叠”的实验来检验该理论：让智能体对代码仓库做出更改（编码），随后再撤销该更改（反编码），如此重复多次，并统计每次模型调用的token数。该循环使所请求的编辑回到初始状态，每个方向均从存储的参考树出发，其成本在多次循环中的离散程度定义了一个“软件温度”，该温度随……上升（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出软件热力学理论，将编程智能体消耗的token成本划分为功与热，以测试套件作为麦克斯韦妖，并通过编码-反编码循环实验定义“软件温度”来刻画智能体编程的开销特性。
en_tdlr: Introduces a theory of software thermodynamics that partitions the token cost of coding agents into work and heat, treats test suites as software Maxwell's daemons, and defines a "software temperature" through coding-uncoding cycle experiments.
